request.prompt:
You are an independent evaluation judge. Grade the proposed remedy, not the
writing style of this prompt. A good remedy changes a concrete future behavior,
is broad enough to cover the failure mode without becoming a platitude, uses a
real `Use when ...` trigger when it is a skill, leaks no evidence-specific
project nouns into the remedy text, and uses the cheapest adequate remedy type.

Score every dimension from 1 (poor) to 5 (excellent). Give exactly one concise
sentence of justification for each score. Do not infer facts that are absent.

PROPOSAL:
{
  "failure_statement": "Explicit task constraints were lost during implementation.",
  "remedy_content": {
    "target": "global",
    "text": "Before making changes, restate and preserve every explicit scope, file, and tool constraint from the request."
  },
  "remedy_type": "claude-md",
  "routing_rationale": "A standing one-line instruction is cheaper than a procedural skill."
}

response.result: {"actionability":{"score":3,"justification":"\"Restate and preserve every explicit constraint\" names a behavior but gives no concrete mechanism (e.g., write it into a task list, re-check before final edit), so compliance is hard to verify."},"generality_without_vagueness":{"score":2,"justification":"The instruction is broad enough to apply to any task but is phrased as a platitude (\"preserve every constraint\") rather than pinpointing the actual failure mechanism (e.g., constraints dropped across long/multi-step edits or context compaction)."},"trigger_quality":{"score":2,"justification":"As a claude-md addition it has no real conditional trigger — \"before making changes\" fires on literally every task, so it can't be selectively surfaced the way a skill's \"Use when...\" clause would be."},"leakage":{"score":5,"justification":"The remedy text contains no project-, file-, or tool-specific nouns — it is fully generic and portable across contexts."},"routing_fitness":{"score":3,"justification":"A one-line global standing instruction is plausibly cheaper than a procedural skill, but the failure statement is too generic to confirm this is the right remedy type versus, e.g., reinforcing existing task-tracking tool use."}}

actionability.justification: "Restate and preserve every explicit constraint" names a behavior but gives no concrete mechanism (e.g., write it into a task list, re-check before final edit), so compliance is hard to verify.

generality_without_vagueness.justification: The instruction is broad enough to apply to any task but is phrased as a platitude ("preserve every constraint") rather than pinpointing the actual failure mechanism (e.g., constraints dropped across long/multi-step edits or context compaction).

leakage.justification: The remedy text contains no project-, file-, or tool-specific nouns — it is fully generic and portable across contexts.

routing_fitness.justification: A one-line global standing instruction is plausibly cheaper than a procedural skill, but the failure statement is too generic to confirm this is the right remedy type versus, e.g., reinforcing existing task-tracking tool use.

trigger_quality.justification: As a claude-md addition it has no real conditional trigger — "before making changes" fires on literally every task, so it can't be selectively surfaced the way a skill's "Use when..." clause would be.
